chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Fazari. He said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi Nuwayra informed us, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Qarn Abu Sulayman al-Dabbi. He said:

Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), sent some of his law enforcement to Lubayd al-Ataridi. They passed by him at the Mosque of Simak. So Na'im ibn Dajaja al-Asadi went to him and intervened between them and him. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) sent for Na'im, and he was brought to him.

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) raised something to strike him. So Na'im said: By God, indeed your companionship is humbling, and indeed opposing you is disbelief. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: And do you know that? He said: Yes. He said: Let him go.

key_terms.خلافك لكفر: Opposing you is disbelief - recognition that opposition to the rightful Imam constitutes rejection of faith
key_terms.شرطه: Shurta - law enforcement officers or police force serving the caliph
key_terms.صحبتك لذل: Your companionship is humbling - acknowledgment that obedience to the Imam, while difficult, is the right path

ai.seo_question: What did Na'im ibn Dajaja say to Imam Ali about obedience and opposition?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts an episode during the caliphate of Imam Ali (AS) in Kufa where Na'im ibn Dajaja al-Asadi obstructed the Imam's police force sent to apprehend Lubayd al-Ataridi. When brought before the Imam and facing punishment, Na'im declared that while following Ali was humbling, opposing him was disbelief. Upon confirming his sincere conviction, Ali pardoned him, demonstrating both the authority of the Imam and his clemency toward those who acknowledge his rightful position.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Fazarani. He said: `Abbad b. Ya`qub narrated to us. He said: Mansur b. Abi Nuwayra informed us from Abi Bakr b. `Ayash from Qarn Abi Sulayman al-Dabi. He said: `

Ali b. Abi Talib (as) sent some law enforcement for Lubayd al-`Ataridi. They passed by him at the Samak Mosque (in Kufa). So, Na`im b. Dajaja al-Asadi went to him and resolved [the issue] between them and him. So, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) sent for Na`im, and he was brought to him.

He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) raised something to strike him. So, Na`im said: Surely, being your companion is humbling, but being your opponent is disbelief. So, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said: Do you know this? He said: Yes. He said: Let him free.
